newsitem.title: USA: BPA lowers firm peak power prices $2/MWh for Mon.
newsitem.headline: BPA lowers firm peak power prices $2/MWh for Mon.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) lowered prices for firm during during peak demand hours on Monday by $2.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the agency said Friday.
BPA still offered up to 300 megawatts of firm peak power on Monday, but lowered prices to $14.75 per MWh for Northwest sales and $15.75 for California-Oregon border (COB) sales.
Prices for non-firm power during shoulder hours on Monday (0600, 1100-1700 and 2100-2200 PST) were cut by $1.00 to $12.00 per MWh for Northwest sales and $13.00 for COB.
BPA continued to refrain from offering non-firm power during morning and evening peaks or any displacement power.
Prices for firm and non-firm power during off-peak hours on Satuday through Monday were unchanged at $9.00 per MWh for all deliveries.
Other prices for Saturday and Sunday were in line with Monday's offers, although peak and off-peak blocks were defined slightly differently.
